circumstances: Bodaboda (motorcycle taxi) driver based at the Mlima CCM stand in Murieti ward, Arusha. He was reported missing in the days before his body was found on Saturday 12 September 2026, dumped inside an unfinished building in the Bondeni area of Murieti, with the throat cut and eyes gouged out; his motorcycle has not been found. After he disappeared, his phone was reportedly found by an unknown person who asked the family to pay TZS 10,000 for its return before cutting off contact. Investigation ongoing; no official confirmation of the perpetrators. (Last-seen date approximate.)

23-year-old young man taken from his home in the Sinza area of Dar es Salaam on the night of 11 September 2026, at about 10:00 PM (saa 4 usiku), by people who had followed him and arrived on motorcycles. According to his maternal aunt (mama mdogo), his body was afterwards seen at Mwananyamala Hospital in Dar es Salaam, where it was reported that he appeared to have been struck on the head with a heavy object. Mwananyamala Hospital management says it does not know who brought the body in, because the person who delivered it did not register and simply abandoned it there — by those accounts the hospital received the body on the night of 12 September 2026. The family is asking whether he was killed during the night of 11 September or on 12 September, and who took his body to the hospital without identifying themselves. (Account as shared publicly by the family and as stated by the hospital; no independent confirmation, and no suspects have been officially named.)

Student. Reportedly abducted by armed men on 27 August 2026 at Bagamoyo, Coast region; the abduction was filmed by residents. He has not been seen since. According to activist Maria Sarungi Tsehai and posts by CHADEMA activist Hilda Newton, the reported motivation was his breakup with his girlfriend Ruiya, daughter of Gwandise Jumanne Kelegele, a security officer whose work station is State House, Dar es Salaam. His mother, Irene Mziray, has publicly appealed to the government for help in locating him.

Bodaboda (motorcycle taxi) driver operating in the Tengeru Kwa Fundi area, Arumeru district, Arusha region. He went missing for several days before his body was discovered in a field at Kitongoji Madira, Singisi village, Sela Singisi ward, Arumeru, bearing multiple injuries including gouged eyes. The landowner found the body while tending his crops in the morning and reported it to the authorities; police collected the body and took it to the mortuary. Investigation ongoing. (Last-seen date approximate.)

High-profile politician and diplomat who served as Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania from November 2025, after a career spanning Minister of Home Affairs, Ambassador to Brazil and Egypt, and Secretary-General of the ruling CCM party. On 25 August 2026 he announced his resignation (effective 4 September 2026), and on 26 August 2026 CCM's Central Committee expelled him from the party, reportedly after he publicly broke ranks to speak out against the state's hard-handed tactics against the political opposition. Within days of stepping down he vanished from public view: former Prime Minister Joseph Sinde Warioba publicly raised concern, saying repeated calls to him went unanswered and his whereabouts were unknown. Tanzanian activists, including Maria Sarungi Tsehai, have reported that he is being held incommunicado under strict house arrest by state security forces, with his electronic devices confiscated — these reports remain unverified, and there has been no official or independent confirmation of his whereabouts or condition. (Day of last public appearance approximate.)

Phone repairman based in Kariakoo, Dar es Salaam. According to activist Maria Sarungi Tsehai, he was abducted by plain-clothes policemen on 12 August 2026 and has not been seen since; she describes him as one of many young men abducted and disappeared into "black sites" since July. A family appeal identifies him as Peter Richard Mushi (35), resident of Yombo Relini, and CCTV footage circulating online purports to show the abduction in Kariakoo. No official confirmation.

Bodaboda (motorcycle taxi) driver based in Kawe, Dar es Salaam, who became the subject of widespread missing-person appeals in August and September 2026. According to public alerts and social-media campaigns shared by his family and activists, on Saturday 1 August 2026 at around 4:00 PM, approximately five individuals arrived at his home in Kawe, identified themselves as police officers, and took him away without explaining where he was being escorted. His whereabouts remain unknown; his pregnant wife has publicly asked for help locating him. No official confirmation.

Personal assistant to jailed CHADEMA chairman Tundu Lissu. On 20 May 2026 around 10 pm, near his home in the Bunju/Mabwepande area of Dar es Salaam, his car was blocked by a Toyota Probox and two motorcycles; five to six men identifying themselves as police officers pulled him out, handcuffed him, beat him with gun butts, and drove him away toward an intelligence-security forest area near Mbweni while pursuing bodaboda riders followed. When the captors stopped to fire on the pursuers, he escaped from the vehicle's boot into the forest and crawled out overnight, arriving home on the morning of 21 May 2026 in poor condition and still handcuffed. His full first-person account was published by The Chanzo; police later issued a statement on the incident.

Well-known minerals businessman in Arusha, popularly known as "Banjoo". Abducted by unidentified people on 12 February 2026 as he was leaving a gym beneath the Ngorongoro building in Arusha. His body was found on 18 February 2026 beside the road in the Bereko area, Kondoa district, Dodoma region, bearing severe injuries: broken arms and gouged eyes.

CHADEMA member living in Geita Mjini, Geita region. According to an alert shared on X and amplified by CHADEMA channels, on 29 November 2025 he was taken by individuals who identified themselves as police officers. Family members and CHADEMA leaders checked local police stations, where they say they received no cooperation and were instead threatened with arrest. His whereabouts remain unknown. No official confirmation.

Chairman of the street vendors (machinga) at the Simu 2000 market in Dar es Salaam — a role confirmed by Tanzanian media including The Citizen. According to alerts shared on X and CHADEMA-aligned pages, on 27 November 2025 he was taken by individuals who identified themselves as police officers. Relatives report checking multiple police stations without finding him. His whereabouts remain unknown. No official confirmation.

Former ambassador and government critic. Reportedly abducted from his home in Dar es Salaam on 6 October 2025; his family reported the incident to police the next morning and his lawyer filed a habeas corpus application.

Frequent government critic on social media. Beaten with a metal bar by unidentified assailants in Dar es Salaam on 16 June 2025 until he lost consciousness; while awaiting hospital surgery, people dressed as doctors entered his room and attacked him again, according to Human Rights Watch.

Kenyan human rights activist. Arrested in Dar es Salaam on 19 May 2025 while attending the treason trial of Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu, held incommunicado and tortured, then released at the Kenya–Tanzania border on 22 May 2025 with signs of severe torture.
Opposition activist, widely known as Mdude. Violently attacked and abducted from his home in Mbeya on the night of 2 May 2025 by unidentified individuals; his whereabouts remain unknown.

Member of the CHADEMA secretariat. Abducted from a bus travelling from Dar es Salaam to Tanga on 6 September 2024 by armed men; his body was found in Ununio, Dar es Salaam, on 7 September 2024 with signs of torture, including acid poured on his face.
CHADEMA youth leader. Abducted by unidentified men in the Buza area, Dar es Salaam, on 18 August 2024, along with two colleagues; remains missing.
CHADEMA opposition leader in Temeke. Abducted alongside Deusdedith Soka and Frank Mbise by unidentified men in the Buza area, Dar es Salaam, on 18 August 2024; remains missing.

Motorcycle taxi driver who worked for CHADEMA activist Deusdedith Soka. Abducted alongside Soka and Jacob Godwin Mlay by unidentified men in the Buza area, Dar es Salaam, on 18 August 2024; remains missing.

Political activist, choir songwriter and composer, and CHADEMA official who served as the party's Secretary of Politics, Ideology and Propaganda for the Rukwa Region. On 26 July 2024, according to family accounts and local reports, he was at home during a family meeting when he received a phone call summoning him to the Central Police Station in Rukwa. He left for the station and never returned; his phone was switched off shortly after. Local police subsequently denied having him in custody. Before his disappearance he was a vocal government critic, notably recording a viral video criticizing the size and extravagance of President Samia Suluhu Hassan's official motorcade during a regional visit to Rukwa and Katavi. CHADEMA leader Tundu Lissu and human-rights organizations have repeatedly demanded investigations into his whereabouts, citing his case as part of a pattern of enforced disappearances targeting opposition figures in Tanzania. (Details per family accounts, The Chanzo and HRW.)

Prominent social-media activist known online as Sativa, and a vocal critic of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party. On 23 June 2024 he was abducted by plainclothes operatives on a highway in Dar es Salaam, held overnight at a local police station, then blindfolded, handcuffed and transported more than 1,000 km across the country. His captors interrogated him about who was facilitating his online activism and his involvement in mobilizing local trader boycotts, and severely beat him with sticks and machetes. Four days later, on 27 June 2024, they dragged him into the remote Katavi National Park, shot him in the head and left him for dead. He survived, and later sought damages from the authorities through his lawyers. (Details per media reports and The Chanzo.)
